title: Mastering The Filtering Bleb: Clinical Evaluation & Management
summary: A clinical guide to evaluating the post-trabeculectomy filtering bleb, balancing filtration efficiency with the prevention of sight-threatening complications. Proper assessment is the cornerstone of long-term IOP control.

sections.title: Definition & Purpose
sections.content: A filtering bleb is a surgically created conjunctival elevation resulting from the flow of aqueous humor through a partial-thickness scleral flap (trabeculectomy). Its goal is to provide controlled subconjunctival aqueous drainage to achieve target intraocular pressure (IOP) and stabilize glaucomatous damage.

sections.title: The INDIANA BLEB APPEARANCE GRADING SCALE (IBAGS)

content.explanation: P: Position (sup vs inf), O: Opacification/Cystic changes, W: Vascularity (Weight/Engorgement), E: Extent/Elevation, R: Rheology (Seidel sign/leakage).

sections.title: Clinical Red Flags
content: Positive Seidel test: Risk of endophthalmitis
Thin, 'cystic' bleb: High risk of bleb leak/infection
Encapsulated (Tenon's) cyst: Elevated IOP despite surgery

sections.title: Management Algorithm for Dysfunctional Blebs
content: Step 1: Digital ocular massage (if IOP high, no leak)
Step 2: Laser suture lysis (if flap is overtight)
Step 4: Needling revision with subconjunctival anti-metabolites
Step 5: Surgical revision (re-fashioning flap or excision of fibrosis)

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Use fluorescein staining to detect occult leaks not visible under white light.
Superior blebs are generally more successful than inferior blebs due to lid-covered tear distribution.
Avoid excessive topical steroids early post-op to allow controlled fibrosis, unless intense inflammation is noted.
Always evaluate the bleb in primary gaze AND with the eyelid lifted to assess the full extent.

sections.title: Landmark Research Updates
sections.content: Recent evidence from the Tube Versus Trabeculectomy (TVT) study underscores that while bleb-based surgery offers superior pressure reduction, the longevity depends heavily on the 'bleb-maintenance' regimen. Newer studies focus on utilizing subconjunctival collagen matrix implants to modulate bleb scarring without the risks associated with intra-operative Mitomycin-C.
